nagoya_shogetsu_shikemichi.gf_detail: Tempura batter is made with wheat flour — the core product is not gluten-free. No gluten-free batter option is documented. Soy-based dipping sauce (tentsuyu) typically contains wheat soy sauce. No dedicated fryer information found. Celiac diners should not assume safety here without direct confirmation from the kitchen.
nagoya_shogetsu_shikemichi.vegan_detail: Standard tempura restaurant with no published vegan menu. Traditional dashi likely contains katsuobushi (bonito flakes). Vegetable tempura items exist — including mountain vegetables and avocado — but no vegan-declared preparation. Ask well in advance if ordering a vegetable-only course.
nagoya_shogetsu_shikemichi.notes: [Mom & Pop] Owner Kuwahara Sachihide ran a long-established tempura restaurant in Sakae before opening this branch in the historic Nagono/Shikemichi district. He chose the neighbourhood deliberately, drawn by its revival energy and diverse clientele — families, tourists, and locals — distinc

chef_bio.origin: Nagoya, Aichi (branch of the Shogetsu group; Sakae original location predates this Shikemichi branch)
chef_bio.background: Owner Kuwahara Sachihide ran a long-established tempura restaurant in Sakae before opening this branch in the historic Nagono/Shikemichi district. He chose the neighbourhood deliberately, drawn by its revival energy and diverse clientele — families, tourists, and locals — distinct from the suit-and-tie crowd of Sakae.
chef_bio.philosophy: Head chef Tone, with 38 years of tempura experience, uses a thin, delicate batter and a proprietary blend of light corn oil to achieve a crisp, non-greasy result. The restaurant breaks convention by pairing tempura with wine — champagne, Sauvignon Blanc, Bordeaux — rather than defaulting to beer or sake.
chef_bio.specialty: Nori-wrapped yuba and uni (sea urchin) tempura — the house signature — alongside seasonal vegetable tempura and a kakiage rice bowl finish to courses.

anecdotes.text: Kuwahara described his move to Nagono: the old Sakae building had aging issues, but mainly he wanted to ride the wave of new shops opening in this area — hoping the restaurant would help revitalize the Shikemichi streetscape and be enjoyed without being bound by convention.

A blogger visiting in 2017 noted the Kyoto-like townhouse exterior and the U-shaped counter seating 13–14 guests, describing the seaweed-yuba-uni tempura as exceptionally flavorful and the dinner course with wine coming to just over ¥10,000 — 'reasonably priced for a tempura restaurant.'

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: nagono.jpインタビューでオーナー桑原祥秀・料理長刀根清和（天ぷら歴38年）・栄から那古野への移転・薄い衣と独自のコーン油ブレンド・シャンパン/ソーヴィニヨン/ボルドーとのワインペアリング・海苔×湯葉×北海道産ウニの名物天ぷらを確認。2017年ブログで京町家風の外観、13〜14席のU字カウンター、ワイン付きディナー約1万円強を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Tempura is the sole product of this restaurant; wheat-flour batter is used for all items in shared oil. No gluten-free fryer or batter alternative is documented anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Tentsuyu dipping sauce is standard at tempura restaurants and typically contains wheat-based soy sauce. No tamari or GF soy sauce option is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All items are fried in the same oil as seafood (shrimp, uni, etc.). Vegetable tempura shares the fryer with fish and shellfish.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy handling policy or allergen menu is published. Reservation-first model (phone ahead) means dietary requests can be communicated in advance at 070-8960-4649 or 052-485-4410.

positives.text: Counter seating directly faces the chef, making real-time communication about ingredients more practical than in a table-service setting.
Dinner courses are prix-fixe and made-to-order at the counter, which in principle allows ingredient substitutions if discussed when booking.

cultural_comfort.note: A refined counter-only tempura restaurant conducted in Japanese; no English menu or staff language noted — some prior Japanese or confident pointing experience will help.

nagoya_gra_ce_a.gf_detail: No gluten-free menu or labeling found. Classic French techniques mean wheat flour, roux-based sauces, and pastry elements are standard. The kitchen explicitly asks guests to declare allergies at reservation time, suggesting some accommodation may be possible, but no dedicated GF protocol or fryer information is published. Japanese soy sauce (contains wheat) is commonly used in fusion French cooking. Celiacs should contact the restaurant before booking — do not assume safety.
nagoya_gra_ce_a.vegan_detail: No dedicated vegan menu. French cuisine with seasonal Japanese ingredients; dishes include foie gras, duck, fish, and dairy. The restaurant states that allergy and dietary restrictions must be communicated at reservation time — same-day changes cannot be accommodated. There is no published vegan course. Hidden animal-based ingredients (butter, cream, dashi-style stocks) are likely throughout. Vegans should inquire thoroughly before booking.
nagoya_gra_ce_a.hours_raw: Mon, Wed–Sun & holidays 11:30–14:30 (L.O. 13:30), 18:00–22:00 (dinner single simultaneous start at 18:30). Closed Tue.
nagoya_gra_ce_a.notes: Chef Ishida Katsuhisa opened grâce à… independently on October 13, 2025, after building his career at several notable Nagoya establishments including Chez Wada Koraibridge (closed), Bistro da Ange, Auberge de l'Ill Nagoya (a prestigious Hiramatsu-group French restaurant), and Lux

chef_bio.origin: Nagoya, Aichi, Japan. Opened October 13, 2025 in a compact 10-seat space (a 6-seat counter plus two tables of two) in the Shuttle Asama (シャトル浅間) building, Nishi Ward, a 3-minute walk from Asama-cho Station.
chef_bio.background: Chef Ishida Katsuhisa opened grâce à… as his own independent restaurant on October 13, 2025. Detailed public documentation of his earlier career is scarce, but the cooking on the plate reflects a seasoned French hand working a tiny counter kitchen with a daily-changing, market-driven menu.
chef_bio.philosophy: The restaurant name grâce à means 'thanks to' in French — the concept centers on gratitude: each dish is framed as an expression of appreciation to customers, producers, and suppliers.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal multi-course French cuisine integrating premium Japanese regional ingredients — dishes have included Iwate black abalone, Hokkaido duck breast with citrus (Mikawa mandarin) sauce, Noto Peninsula stone bream with bamboo shoots (takenoko), and Hungarian foie gras mousse with Aomori apple.

anecdotes.text: A blog post from early 2026 detailed a dinner featuring snow crab and celeriac mousse with crab-liver flan and caviar, Iwate abalone with sea urchin, and Hokkaido lily-root blancmange — all reflecting the chef's hallmark of layering French technique over seasonal Japanese produce.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ・ホットペッパーが2025年10月13日開業、西区幅下（シャトル浅間1F）、全10席（カウンター6席＋2名卓×2）を確認。アメブロの実食記事がシェフ名（石田克久）と、フレンチ技法×国産季節食材の皿を裏付ける。開業以前の詳しい経歴を記す公開情報は見当たらなかった。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No dedicated gluten-free kitchen or cross-contamination protocol is published. Classic French preparations routinely use wheat flour in sauces, pastry, and coatings.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No mention of tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternatives. French-Japanese fusion cooking at this level commonly incorporates regular soy sauce (which contains wheat) in marinades and sauces.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Animal products (butter, cream, meat stocks, seafood) are central to the cuisine; vegan cross-contact is highly probable given the 10-seat kitchen with no vegan-specific protocol.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The restaurant explicitly requires allergy and dietary restriction disclosure at the time of reservation ('ご予約時にアレルギーなどNG食材を必ずお伝えください'). Same-day menu changes are not accepted.

positives.text: Pre-reservation allergy declaration policy means the chef is made aware of restrictions before cooking begins, giving the best chance of accommodation within a French tasting-menu format.

cultural_comfort.note: Intimate 10-seat counter-focused restaurant run by a single chef; Japanese is the working language and reservations require allergy/restriction communication in advance — English speakers should use a translation tool or ask a Japanese-speaking friend to call ahead.

nagoya_seisei.gf_detail: No gluten-free claim is made. The noodles use a blend of first- and second-grade buckwheat flour; the ratio of buckwheat to wheat binder is unconfirmed — they may not be 100% buckwheat (juwari). The tsuyu dipping sauce almost certainly contains wheat-based soy sauce. Tempura is on the menu and shares kitchen space, creating cross-contamination risk. Anyone with celiac disease should call ahead (052-531-2814) before visiting and cannot assume safety.
nagoya_seisei.vegan_detail: Not vegan. Signature toppings include herring (ニシン), salmon roe (イクラ), and quail egg (鶉卵). The dipping broth is almost certainly fish-based (bonito/katsuo dashi), and standard wheat soy sauce is used throughout. No vegan alternatives are listed anywhere.
nagoya_seisei.notes: [Mom & Pop] A neighbourhood soba shop that has stood near Asama-cho Station in Nagoya's Nishi Ward for at least four decades — the restaurant appears in Nagoya dining guides from the mid-1980s. It is run as a small family business, reputedly by an elderly couple assisted by a single server.

chef_bio.origin: Nishi Ward, Nagoya; active since at least the mid-1980s
chef_bio.background: A neighbourhood soba shop that has stood near Asama-cho Station in Nagoya's Nishi Ward for at least four decades — the restaurant appears in Nagoya dining guides from the mid-1980s. It is run as a small family business, reputedly by an elderly couple assisted by a single server.
chef_bio.philosophy: Quality everyday soba made with carefully selected first- and second-grade buckwheat flour; strongly textured, aromatic noodles served with an unusually generous range of condiments at an accessible price.
chef_bio.specialty: Tenzaru Seisei Soba — cold buckwheat noodles presented across five stacked lacquer trays, accompanied by eight distinct condiments: wasabi, shredded nori, quail egg, salmon roe, herring, matsumae pickles, mountain vegetables, and grated nameko mushroom, alongside a tempura assortment and a light, subtly sweet dipping broth.

anecdotes.text: The restaurant has been listed in Nagoya print guidebooks since the mid-1980s, making it one of the longer-standing soba spots in this part of the city.
The eight-condiment presentation — ニシン, イクラ, 鶉卵, 松前漬け, 山菜, 滑子颪, 刻み海苔, 山葵 — served across five stacked trays is the dish most frequently photographed and cited by visitors.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Tempura is a core menu item; no separate fryer is indicated. Shared frying oil is a realistic cross-contamination risk for anyone avoiding gluten.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned on any listing. Standard (wheat-containing) soy sauce is almost certainly used in the tsuyu dipping broth and any seasoned dishes.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish-based dashi (bonito) is the expected base for the tsuyu broth at a traditional soba restaurant of this type; no plant-based alternative is indicated.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy-handling policy is described on any source. Japanese-only communication is expected; calling ahead at 052-531-2814 is strongly advised for anyone with dietary restrictions.

positives.text: Buckwheat (soba) noodles are naturally gluten-free in their pure form; the restaurant's emphasis on quality flour is noted, though the exact buckwheat-to-wheat blend ratio is undisclosed.

cultural_comfort.note: A long-running neighbourhood soba shop; menus and staff communication are in Japanese only, with no indication of English service.

nagoya_ashita_no_tame_no_shijim.gf_detail: Standard Japanese izakaya with no documented gluten-free options. The oden broth is shijimi (clam) based, but wheat-containing soy sauce (醤油) is standard in Japanese oden broth and grilled skewers. Grilled items (備長炭焼き) may use marinades with wheat soy sauce. No dedicated GF menu, fryer, or allergy menu was found across any source. Celiacs should call ahead; safe options cannot be confirmed without direct kitchen inquiry.
nagoya_ashita_no_tame_no_shijim.vegan_detail: The restaurant's defining ingredient is shijimi (freshwater clam) dashi, used throughout oden and hot pot preparations. Oysters feature prominently. No plant-based or vegan menu track exists; hidden animal-derived dashi is virtually guaranteed in every dish. Anyone avoiding seafood and shellfish will find almost nothing suitable without direct kitchen negotiation.
nagoya_ashita_no_tame_no_shijim.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00 (L.O. 23:00), closed Sun (some sources say open daily). Lunch service available (some sources: 11:30–13:30). Closed over New Year period (Jan 1–4, or through Jan 5).
nagoya_ashita_no_tame_no_shijim.notes: [Mom & Pop] The main branch of Shijimibaka opened in September 2019 in Nagoya's Nishiki entertainment district (Sakae), founded by representative Tsuda with a mission the name encapsulates: shijimi (freshwater clams) are rich in ornithine, which supports liver function and recovery — so toni

chef_bio.origin: 名古屋市中区錦 (main branch); 名古屋市東区泉 (this branch, opened May 2023)
chef_bio.background: The main branch of Shijimibaka opened in September 2019 in Nagoya's Nishiki entertainment district (Sakae), founded by representative Tsuda with a mission the name encapsulates: shijimi (freshwater clams) are rich in ornithine, which supports liver function and recovery — so tonight's izakaya dinner becomes fuel for tomorrow rather than a drain on it. The group crowdfunded in late 2020 to expand into e-commerce (shijimi shoyu, ponzu, vending machines). The Izumi/久屋大通 branch opened in May 2023, 5 minutes from Hisaya Odori Station, and draws a strong office-worker lunch crowd alongside its evening izakaya trade.
chef_bio.philosophy: The brand positions shijimi as a health-supporting food: its ornithine content is thought to aid liver recovery and sleep quality, so the concept frames indulgent izakaya dining as genuinely restorative — 'tomorrow's vitality, tonight. '
chef_bio.specialty: しじみ出汁おでん（clam-broth oden）, especially the げんこつ大根 (giant daikon slow-cooked over two days in clam broth), and the しじみエスプレッソ (concentrated clam essence as an amuse-bouche).

anecdotes.text: The main-branch shijimi dashi earned a Japan Food Selection Gold Award, and the restaurant parlayed that recognition into a crowdfunding campaign to sell bottled shijimi shoyu and build what it called 'the world's first shijimi dashi vending machines' for entertainment districts.
The signature げんこつ大根 (fist daikon) takes two full days of preparation in clam broth before it reaches the table.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No dedicated GF preparation area or fryer documented. Standard izakaya kitchen — cross-contamination from wheat via soy sauce, marinades, and shared cooking surfaces must be assumed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Shijimi dashi broth is the restaurant's specialty, but conventional wheat-containing soy sauce (醤油) is standard in Japanese oden broth and yakitori marinades. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative was documented anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Shijimi (clam) dashi is the foundational stock used across virtually all dishes. Oysters are a featured menu item. No plant-only cooking zone exists.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy menu, allergy questionnaire, or staff training documentation was found in any source. Guests with serious food allergies should call ahead (052-228-3531) before visiting.

positives.text: The core broth is made from shijimi (freshwater clams), not from wheat-containing or fermented products — so the broth base itself may be inherently wheat-light, though the soy sauce used to season it almost certainly contains wheat unless tamari is specifically requested.

cultural_comfort.note: A local izakaya with Japanese-language menus and no noted English support; basic Japanese or a translation app is useful here.

nagoya_hitsumabushi_togawa_nago.gf_detail: The eel kabayaki glaze is soy-sauce-based (contains wheat), and the dashi and tare for the hitsumabushi likely also contain wheat. No gluten-free menu or information on whether ingredients can be omitted has been confirmed. Not suitable for people with celiac disease or wheat allergy.
nagoya_hitsumabushi_togawa_nago.vegan_detail: The menu is based on charcoal-grilled eel, chicken, Nagoya Cochin eggs, and bonito dashi; there are no plant-only options.
nagoya_hitsumabushi_togawa_nago.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–14:30 (L.O. 14:00) and 17:30–22:00 (L.O. 21:30); Sat, Sun, holidays 11:30–15:00 (L.O. 14:30) and 17:30–22:00 (L.O. 21:30); closed Wed (also closed Dec 31 and Jan 1)
nagoya_hitsumabushi_togawa_nago.notes: Opened in November 2020 in the Shikemichi area of Nagono, Nagoya. Set in a renovated roughly 90-year-old traditional house, it features a Japanese garden said to be about 320 years old. It shares its grounds with the Japanese restaurant "Nakuon" in the same area. It is operated by Matsuri Group, which also opened Sakae and Ikeshita branches in July 2021.

chef_bio.origin: 名古屋市西区那古野（四間道エリア）
chef_bio.background: 2020年11月、名古屋・那古野の四間道エリアに開業。 築約90年の古民家を改装した建物で、約320年と伝わる日本庭園を眺めながら食事ができる。 同じ敷地内の日本料理店「懐韻（かいいん）」と敷地を共有している。 運営は祭りグループ（Matsuri Group）で、栄店・池下店も展開する（池下店は2021年7月、池下セントラルガーデン内に開業）。
chef_bio.philosophy: 「お客様全員が満足できるものだけを追求し、提供する」（大森シェフ）。 季節ごとに最上質のうなぎを仕入れ、備長炭で焼き上げる。 米は岐阜県産「にこまる」を使用。
chef_bio.specialty: 炭火焼きひつまぶし・中黄金うな重（炭焼きうなぎ×名古屋コーチン卵のだし巻き玉子の組み合わせ）

anecdotes.text: 四間道の歴史的な町並みに溶け込む古民家の佇まいと、約320年と伝わる日本庭園を眺めながら食事できる空間が特徴。円頓寺商店街と外堀通をつなぐ通りに面する。
看板メニュー「中黄金うな重」は、炭焼きうなぎと名古屋コーチン卵のだし巻き玉子を一度に味わえる一品として人気を集めている。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 情報通・食べログ・ヒトサラで、2020年11月開業、築約90年の古民家、約320年の日本庭園、岐阜県産にこまる、備長炭、中黄金うな重を確認。ヒトサラでシェフ名（大森光記）を確認。祭りグループ公式サイトで那古野本店・栄店・池下店の3店舗展開と池下店の2021年7月開業を確認。隣接店は「懐韻」。

gf_cross_contamination.text: うなぎの蒲焼きタレ・ひつまぶしの出汁・かけ汁はいずれも醤油（小麦）ベースと推定される。グルテンフリー対応の代替タレや除去オプションは公式・口コミいずれでも確認できない。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: ひつまぶしの蒲焼きタレは醤油・みりん・砂糖ベースで、一般的なうなぎのタレには小麦由来成分が含まれる。店舗での小麦不使用醤油使用については情報なし。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 全メニューが動物性食材（うなぎ・鶏・卵・鰹だし）を使用しており、植物性食材のみの調理ラインは存在しない。

staff_allergy_handling.text: アレルギー対応・スタッフによる除去対応についての公式案内は確認されていない。来店前に電話（052-526-0063）で直接確認を推奨。

positives.text: 完全禁煙。個室あり（2〜4名・4〜6名・VIP 4〜8名）。テイクアウト・デリバリー（Uber Eats）にも対応しており、持ち帰りで自宅での成分確認が可能。

cultural_comfort.note: 予約・注文はほぼ日本語のみ対応；英語メニューや英語スタッフの情報は確認されていない。

nagoya_caffe_cammello.gf_detail: The cafe's identity is built around house-baked wheat bread (focaccia, ciabatta) — gluten is central to the menu. No gluten-free bread alternative or GF-designated item is mentioned on the official site, Tabelog, HotPepper, or any blog. Coffee drinks may be wheat-free in isolation, but cross-contamination risk is high in a bread-focused kitchen. Not appropriate for celiac diners.
nagoya_caffe_cammello.vegan_detail: No vegan-designated menu items. The food menu centers on house-baked focaccia and ciabatta sandwiches with fillings such as smoked salmon, chicken fillet, and mozzarella; desserts include scones made with fermented butter, brownies, and flan cake. Dairy and meat are standard throughout. No evidence of dairy-free or egg-free alternatives. Evening bar service includes wine and whiskey. Ask staff if any drink or simple item can be prepared without animal products.
nagoya_caffe_cammello.hours_raw: Mon/Tue 08:00–20:00 (L.O. 19:30), Wed–Sun & holidays 11:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:30), open daily (temporary closures announced on social media)
nagoya_caffe_cammello.notes: [Mom & Pop] Caffe CAMMELLO opened on 10 March 2020 in the quiet residential neighbourhood of Kaminagoya, a 10-minute walk from Joshin Station on the Tsurumai Line. The café's Wix profile is registered under the username tanakateruyuki38, pointing to an owner named Tanaka Teruyuki, though thi

chef_bio.origin: 名古屋市西区上名古屋, Nagoya
chef_bio.background: Caffe CAMMELLO opened on 10 March 2020 in the quiet residential neighbourhood of Kaminagoya, Nishi Ward, a 10-minute walk from Joshin Station on the Tsurumai Line. It is run by an owner-operator documented only as 'the master' (マスター). The name Cammello is Italian for camel, rendered in a logo that appears on the glass door.
chef_bio.philosophy: The cafe styles itself as a calm hideaway where quietly flowing jazz is the backdrop to unhurried time — coffee, sandwiches, and desserts crafted with care, 'turning quality beans into the finest cup we can.'
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-dripped coffee from carefully selected beans; house-baked focaccia and ciabatta sandwiches

anecdotes.text: The seasonal fruit open sandwich — layered with whipped cream, vanilla ice cream, hazelnut spread, and Edam cheese — illustrates the kitchen's playful approach to a café staple.
Baked goods including scones and brownies are sold at Ion Town Meisei (the 'Wakuwaku Hiroba' marketplace) in addition to the café, extending the kitchen's reach into the neighbourhood.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト・食べログで2020年3月10日開業、名古屋市西区上名古屋、浄心駅徒歩約10分、全16席（カウンター6・ソファ10）、自家焙煎珈琲と自家製フォカッチャ/チャバタのサンド、イオンタウン名西での焼き菓子販売を確認。店主名は「マスター」以上の記載なし。

gf_cross_contamination.text: House-baked wheat bread (focaccia, ciabatta) is the core product; flour is actively used throughout the kitchen. Cross-contamination risk for gluten is high and no GF protocols are documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Butter, dairy, and eggs appear throughout the baked-goods and sandwich menu; no vegan-safe preparation areas noted.

cultural_comfort.note: Small independent neighborhood cafe with no English signage noted; basic Japanese helpful for ordering, but the relaxed atmosphere and simple menu make it approachable.

nagoya_shunzen_wada.gf_detail: No gluten-free information published anywhere. Japanese cuisine at this level routinely uses wheat-based soy sauce (shoyu) in marinades, sauces, and simmered dishes. No dedicated GF fryer or GF menu noted. Cross-contamination risk is unquantifiable. With celiac disease or severe wheat allergy, inquire through your introducer before booking — there is no public channel to ask.
nagoya_shunzen_wada.vegan_detail: No vegan or vegetarian information published anywhere. The omakase is built around seasonal seafood, land animals (Ena chicken, Miharu beef, eel), and chef-grown vegetables. Dashi almost certainly uses katsuobushi or similar fish-based stock. No sources mention vegan accommodation. With advance notice via your introducer, a custom course may be negotiable, but nothing is confirmed.
nagoya_shunzen_wada.hours_raw: Fully reservation-only, irregular operation. Open only on days with reservations. Around 18:00.
nagoya_shunzen_wada.notes: [Mom & Pop] Wada trained for 16 years across three Japanese restaurants in Nagoya before making an unexpected detour into farming. He returned to the kitchen carrying both the discipline of a seasoned itamae and the hands-on knowledge of someone who has grown his own food. He opened Shunzen

chef_bio.background: Wada trained for 16 years across three Japanese restaurants in Nagoya before making an unexpected detour into farming. He returned to the kitchen carrying both the discipline of a seasoned itamae and the hands-on knowledge of someone who has grown his own food. He opened Shunzen Wada in June 2016 in Nagoya's Marunouchi district.
chef_bio.philosophy: The restaurant exists to maximize the flavour of ingredients at their peak. Wada explains each dish's ingredients and technique to diners as they eat, turning the counter into something reviewers have called 'Wada Theater. ' Every detail — cuisine, sake, space — is under his direct control.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal omakase built on chef-grown vegetables and hyper-local sourcing — signature dishes have included charcoal-grilled natural ayu in a ceramic bowl, bowl of grated taro with shark fin, and Nagara River sweetfish.

anecdotes.text: Reservations through December 2026 were nearly full by early 2026, with the next opening date for January 2027 bookings announced for March 1, 2026 — remarkable for a restaurant that serves essentially one party per night.
Gault&Millau awarded Shunzen Wada a score of 14/20, recognising the chef's focus on vegetables he cultivates personally and his practice of narrating each dish's story to diners.

The interior was designed by Torii Yoshinori of Torii Design Office and featured in the January 2018 issue of 商店建築 (Shotenkenchiku) magazine, with handmade Japanese paper art, custom calligraphy for the sign, and Koizumi Lighting's bespoke lighting scheme.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No published information on soy sauce type used. At this style of Japanese omakase, wheat-containing soy sauce is standard unless a chef explicitly uses tamari or GF alternatives — none mentioned anywhere.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy handling policy is publicly documented. Given the referral-only, single-party-per-night format, dietary needs would need to be communicated through the introducer at the time of booking.

positives.text: One chef, one small party per night — if dietary needs are communicated in advance through an introducer, the format theoretically allows for fully customised preparation. No shared fryer risk from other tables.

cultural_comfort.note: Entirely referral-only with no public address or phone number; all communication is in Japanese and requires an introducer's name and contact information — not accessible without an existing Japanese-speaking connection to the restaurant.

nagoya_owari_sui_inaba.gf_detail: No gluten-free menu exists. Wheat is embedded in standard preparations: soy sauce (koikuchi) in kappo seasoning, tempura batter (wheat flour) for the tempura counter, and likely wheat-containing dashi or sauces. The restaurant asks that allergy concerns be raised before the visit and explicitly states it may decline to accommodate requests for safety reasons. Not suitable for celiac without advance discussion and acceptance of uncertainty.
nagoya_owari_sui_inaba.vegan_detail: Standard kaiseki and tempura menus are built around seafood, fish dashi (bonito/kombu), and meat — no plant-based course is offered. Hidden animal-derived elements (katsuo dashi, fish-based broths) appear throughout. Inquire well in advance; same-day modifications are not possible.
nagoya_owari_sui_inaba.hours_raw: Breakfast 8:00– (weekends/holidays) / 10:00– (weekdays, reservation required); Tempura lunch 11:30–14:00 (LO 13:00); Kappo lunch 12:00–14:30; Dinner (kappo) 17:30–01:00 (food LO 00:00); Tempura dinner 17:30– / 20:30– by reservation
nagoya_owari_sui_inaba.notes: Chef Inaba Masanobu built his career at some of Japan's most prestigious hotel kitchens: he joined Grand Hyatt Tokyo's sushi restaurant 六緑 as sous chef, then led the opening of Conrad Tokyo's Japanese restaurant 風花, becoming executive chef in 2010. In 2016 he moved to Aman Nemu i

roles: Concept chef: 稲葉正信 (Inaba Masanobu)
Kappo counter chef: 大島一真 (Oshima Kazuma)
chef_bio.origin: Tokyo; kappo chef 大島一真 (Oshima Kazuma) from Shima City, Mie Prefecture
chef_bio.background: Chef Inaba Masanobu built his career at some of Japan's most prestigious hotel kitchens: he joined Grand Hyatt Tokyo's sushi restaurant 六緑 as sous chef, then led the opening of Conrad Tokyo's Japanese restaurant 風花, becoming executive chef in 2010. In 2016 he moved to Aman Nemu in Ise-Shima as executive chef, where his breakfast program was cited by US magazine Brides as one of the world's best hotel breakfasts. He received the Cultural Affairs Agency Director's Award in 2014 for promoting Japanese cuisine internationally. In 2021 he opened Ginza Inaba in Tokyo under his own name. Owari Sui Inaba opened October 1, 2025 as the Nagoya outpost inside Espacio Nagoya Castle, with Kazuma Oshima heading the kappo counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: 融通無碍 — adaptability and total hospitality. Inaba frames cooking as 温故知新 (honoring tradition while embracing innovation), freely incorporating luxury ingredients like truffle without sliding into fusion. Oshima's approach centers on reading the room: timing, temperature, and each guest's appetite shape the pace of the meal.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal omakase kappo courses; a signature asagohan (morning kaiseki) featuring handmade tofu, chef-rolled tamagoyaki prepared at the counter, and charcoal-grilled fish; tempura as a parallel counter experience

anecdotes.text: Chef Inaba's breakfast at Aman Nemu was named one of the world's best hotel breakfasts by US magazine Brides — a distinction that directly shaped the morning kaiseki concept at Owari Sui Inaba.
Chef Oshima described his concept of luxury as 'consistent execution of fundamentals,' concluding that true hospitality is created through sensory engagement rather than spectacle.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The tempura counter uses wheat-flour batter as a core element of every course; cross-contamination with shared kitchen equipment is highly likely.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard Japanese soy sauce (containing wheat) is used throughout the kappo menu for seasoning, sauces, and marinades — no gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish dashi (bonito/kombu) is foundational to the kappo cuisine style; plant-based dashi is not indicated anywhere in the menu descriptions.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The restaurant requires allergy disclosure before the visit and states it may decline to accommodate requests in order to prioritize guest safety; same-day changes are not possible.

positives.text: Allergy information is formally collected at reservation stage, giving the kitchen advance notice to plan or decline gracefully.

cultural_comfort.note: High-end kappo counter inside a luxury hotel; counter dining is intimate and paced by the chef — basic Japanese or prior kaiseki experience helps, though hotel staff may assist in English.

nagoya_kissa_sakura.gf_detail: This is a traditional Showa-era kissaten with no GF awareness documented. Toast, sandwiches, pilaf, yakisoba, curry, and spaghetti all contain wheat. The 珈琲わらびもち is made from warabiko (bracken starch) which is inherently GF, but it is prepared in a kitchen handling wheat throughout and no dedicated equipment or protocols are in place. Standard soy sauce (wheat-containing) is expected in savory dishes. Cross-contamination risk is high. Not appropriate for celiac diners.
nagoya_kissa_sakura.vegan_detail: Standard kissaten menu centered on coffee, toast, sandwiches (ham, tuna, egg), pilaf, yakisoba, and curry — all likely contain animal products. The signature 珈琲わらびもち includes whipped cream and kinako; the 珈琲大福 contains cream filling. No vegan-labeled or plant-based items identified. Dashi base in soup items unconfirmed but almost certainly fish-based in a traditional kissaten. Ask at the counter if you need clarification.
nagoya_kissa_sakura.notes: [Mom & Pop] 喫茶さくら operates as the direct-managed café arm of 倉田コーヒー (Kurata Coffee), a specialty coffee roaster from Nagoya's Nishi Ward with over 50 years of history. The café has occupied the ground floor of the 桜華会館 (Oukakkaikan) — a civic hall in Nagoya's government district near the Aic

roles: Directly managed café of Kurata Coffee roastery
chef_bio.origin: 名古屋市中区三の丸、桜華会館 1F
chef_bio.background: 喫茶さくら operates as the direct-managed café arm of 倉田コーヒー (Kurata Coffee), a self-roasting specialty coffee shop from Nagoya's Nishi Ward with about 50 years of history. Founded around 1975 (Shōwa 50), the café occupies the ground floor of the 桜華会館 (Ōkakaikan) — a civic hall in Nagoya's government district (Sannomaru) near the Aichi Prefectural Gokoku Shrine — serving the salarymen and civil servants of the surrounding ministerial precinct.
chef_bio.philosophy: Unchanged Showa hospitality: generous, well-priced plates, a complimentary candy on the way out, and coffee quality anchored by a veteran roaster's beans.
chef_bio.specialty: 珈琲わらびもち — a house invention pairing the soft, jiggly texture of traditional bracken-starch warabimochi with the roastery's own coffee, topped with kinako, fruit, and whipped cream; and 珈琲大福, a coffee-cream-and-bean-paste filled mochi with a moderately sweet character.

anecdotes.text: The café's Showa-to-early-Heisei glassware is still in daily service, and the wooden sugar dispensers have been worn smooth by decades of use — details that food writers single out as signs of an authentic, unchanged kissaten.
A complimentary candy is handed to guests at checkout, and light meals arrive with a small salad — small Showa-era hospitality touches that have become part of the café's identity.
Reviewers describe it as 'the area's only coffee shop' — a solitary outpost in an administrative district otherwise devoid of independent cafés.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 名古屋めしの2記事で、倉田コーヒー直営、西区で約50年の自家焙煎、昭和50年頃創業、桜華会館1F、珈琲わらびもち・珈琲大福、昭和〜平成初期のグラスや使い込まれた木製シュガーポット、退店時の飴サービスを確認。食べログのレビューが「この界隈唯一の喫茶店」と評する。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No GF protocols documented. The kitchen handles wheat continuously across toast, sandwiches, yakisoba, curry, and spaghetti. Cross-contamination risk for celiac diners is high.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard (wheat-containing) soy sauce is expected in savory dishes such as yakisoba and pilaf; no tamari or GF soy sauce alternatives have been documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All cooking takes place in a shared kitchen with animal products throughout the menu; no vegan-separated prep documented.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy-handling procedures, allergen menus, or English-language communication capability have been documented. Phone reservations are accepted (052-203-1900), which may allow advance allergy enquiry in Japanese.

positives.text: The 珈琲わらびもち uses warabiko (bracken starch), which is naturally gluten-free as an ingredient — though kitchen cross-contamination applies.

cultural_comfort.note: A classic government-district kissaten with no English menu or signage; comfortable for Japanese speakers, but very approachable with pointing — counter seating and a simple menu mean ordering is straightforward.

nagoya_soba_dokoro_kikyo.gf_detail: Soba noodles are made from Hokkaido buckwheat flour (naturally gluten-free grain), but the tsuyu dipping sauce and hot broth contain wheat-based soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) as standard. Tenkasu (tempura scraps) are offered as a broth add-in and contain wheat. No dedicated gluten-free menu or allergen labeling was found. The kitchen handles wheat extensively. Cross-contamination risk is significant. Those with celiac disease should contact the restaurant in advance; mild gluten sensitivity may be able to negotiate a plain mori soba with separate accompaniments, but nothing is guaranteed.
nagoya_soba_dokoro_kikyo.vegan_detail: No vegan menu exists. Standard soba tsuyu (dipping broth) is made with katsuo (bonito) dashi, which is not vegan. Fish-based dashi is standard throughout Japanese-style side dishes. The restaurant states it tries to accommodate dietary preferences on request, so advance inquiry is worth attempting, but hidden fish stock in most dishes makes vegan eating here very difficult without explicit pre-arrangement.
nagoya_soba_dokoro_kikyo.notes: [Mom & Pop] そば処 桔梗 is an established soba izakaya in Nagoya's Marunouchi business district, drawing a loyal weekday crowd of office workers and sake enthusiasts. The restaurant operates a main floor and a separate annex (Hanare) — a 160-year-old historic building offering fully private, rese

chef_bio.background: そば処 桔梗 is an established soba izakaya in Nagoya's Marunouchi business district, drawing a loyal weekday crowd of office workers and sake enthusiasts. The restaurant operates a main floor and a separate annex (Hanare) — a 160-year-old historic building offering fully private, reservation-only dining in a space that feels worlds away from the surrounding city.
chef_bio.philosophy: The kitchen pursues 'truly delicious food' through daily sourcing from Yanagibashi Market, adapting the menu to what is freshest. Staff aim to accommodate individual guest preferences — including dietary needs — within the traditional Japanese framework.
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-pulled soba made fresh each morning from Hokkaido buckwheat flour, prized for its fragrant aroma and smooth texture. Served with Shinshu-origin spicy grated daikon. The lunch mori soba and two-color soba set are signature offerings, while evenings expand into seasonal seafood sourced daily from Yanagibashi Central Market.

anecdotes.text: A regular diner noted that warm kake soba mutes the buckwheat's signature fragrance, and recommends ordering cold mori soba to fully appreciate the freshly-milled Hokkaido flour — a distinction the kitchen itself seems to share, given how prominently it features the noodles' aroma in its own description.
The Hanare annex, housed in a 160-year-old building a short walk from the main restaurant, is available for fully private group reservations — a rare offering in Nagoya's downtown core.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The kitchen handles wheat flour extensively — tsuyu broth uses wheat soy sauce, tenkasu (tempura scraps) are offered as a standard broth topping, and wheat-containing dishes are prepared throughout service. Cross-contamination risk for celiac diners is high and unquantified.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard Japanese koikuchi soy sauce (wheat-containing) is the expected base for tsuyu dipping broth and hot soba broth at this style of establishment. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere in available sources.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish-based dashi (katsuo/bonito) is the standard stock for soba tsuyu and hot broths in Japanese soba restaurants. Side dishes sourced daily from Yanagibashi Market are likely prepared with fish dashi or other animal products as a matter of course.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The restaurant states on its website that it tries to accommodate guest preferences and dietary needs to the extent possible ('お客様の好み・苦手なものなども出来る限り対応させていただいており'). Advance contact by phone (052-201-1559) is recommended for any dietary restriction.

positives.text: Soba noodles themselves are made from 100% Hokkaido buckwheat flour — buckwheat is naturally gluten-free. Plain soba noodles without broth would be free of gluten at the grain level, though kitchen cross-contamination cannot be excluded.

cultural_comfort.note: Traditional soba izakaya with Japanese-language menus and staff; no English signage mentioned, though the restaurant states it tries to accommodate guest preferences and dietary needs on request.

nagoya_trattoria_tapiro.gf_detail: No gluten-free options are listed or advertised anywhere. The kitchen's signature dishes — stone-oven pizza and handmade pasta — are wheat-based. No dedicated fryer, no GF pasta alternative, and no allergy-accommodation language was found across Tabelog, Hotpepper, Gnavi, or the official site. Wheat cross-contamination is essentially certain given the kitchen focus. Not suitable for celiac diners without direct confirmation from the restaurant.
nagoya_trattoria_tapiro.vegan_detail: No dedicated vegan menu. Stone-oven pizzas and handmade pastas are the focus; cheese and meat feature prominently across the menu. A Margherita pizza could be ordered without cheese, but dairy and animal products are integral to the cuisine. No vegan-specific items were found in any source. Diner should call ahead to discuss options.
nagoya_trattoria_tapiro.notes: [Mom & Pop] Trattoria TAPIRO opened on 15 October 2025 as the second venture from the operator of Caffe CAMMELLO (浄心). The project was born when the owner (known publicly as Kain/カイン) learned that a talented Italian chef he admired was leaving their previous position and decided to launch a

chef_bio.origin: Yanagihara shopping district, Kita Ward, Nagoya. Opened 15 October 2025.
chef_bio.background: Trattoria TAPIRO opened on 15 October 2025 as the second venture from the operator of Caffe CAMMELLO (浄心). The project was born when the owner learned that a talented Italian chef he admired was leaving their previous position and decided to launch a partnership rather than lose access to their cooking.
chef_bio.philosophy: The restaurant aims to be a neighbourhood イドコロ (a place that feels like yours) — welcoming for everyday meals, dates, and celebrations alike, operating through three modes: lunch trattoria, evening restaurant, and after-22:00 wine bar.
chef_bio.specialty: Stone-oven (石窯) pizza — crispy exterior with a chewy, airy interior — alongside handmade pasta and a curated, Italian-focused wine list (rounded out with a few California wines and a whisky selection)

anecdotes.text: The name TAPIRO comes from the Italian word for tapir (バク), an animal associated in Japanese folk belief with good dreams and a sense of security — reflecting the owner's wish for guests to feel safe and at ease.

The owner launched a crowdfunding campaign on CAMPFIRE to help finance the opening, framing the restaurant as a community-facing spot where locals could gather for authentic Italian at accessible prices.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: CAMPFIRE・食べログで、2025年10月15日開業、北区柳原（名城公園駅徒歩7分）、カフェ キャメッロ（浄心）2号店、イタリア人シェフとの協業、石窯ピッツァ・自家製パスタ、TAPIRO＝バク（安眠・安心）の由来、22時以降のワインバー営業を確認。ワインは伊・加州＋ウイスキーの構成。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The kitchen is built around stone-oven pizza and handmade pasta — both wheat-intensive — making flour airborne cross-contamination a near-certainty. No source mentions any GF protocol.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No mention of soy sauce use in any reviewed source, but standard Italian kitchen soy-sauce risk is low; primary wheat risk is from pizza dough and pasta throughout the kitchen.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Cheese and meat are core to almost every menu item; shared prep surfaces and ovens make vegan cross-contact likely.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy handling policy, allergen menu, or accommodation language was found on any platform reviewed. Diners with serious allergies should contact the restaurant directly at 052-325-3699 before visiting.

positives.text: Cards, e-money, and QR payments accepted — no cash-only barrier for international visitors.
Online reservations available and same-day bookings accepted until 21:00, reducing uncertainty for group visits.

cultural_comfort.note: A neighbourhood Italian trattoria; some basic Japanese will help, as no English menus or English-language outreach were found, though the relaxed atmosphere is approachable.

nagoya_nepal_station.gf_detail: Nepalese cuisine is fundamentally rice-based (dal bhat, basmati rice, momo wrappers are wheat), which is more GF-friendly than Indian restaurants that rely on naan. However, naan and wheat-containing dishes are on the menu. No dedicated GF menu or labelling was found in any source. Momo (dumplings) use wheat-flour wrappers. Standard soy sauce (wheat-containing) is not a typical Nepalese condiment, but cross-contamination risk is unconfirmed. Celiac diners should call ahead and ask specifically which dishes are wheat-free.
nagoya_nepal_station.vegan_detail: Tabelog lists a vegetarian menu (ベジタリアンメニューあり) and health/wellness menu. Nepalese cuisine naturally includes many lentil- and vegetable-based dishes (dal, vegetable curry, chatamari with vegetable topping, pani puri). However, no confirmed fully vegan menu exists and some dishes include egg, dairy (raita), or dried fish in side pickles. Ask staff which items are fully plant-based before ordering.
nagoya_nepal_station.notes: Nepal STATION opened in 2017 as what is described as Nagoya's first authentic Nepalese cuisine specialist restaurant. The concept grew from the reality that many so-called Indian curry restaurants in Japan are actually Nepalese-run — this shop drops the Indian-restaurant disguise

chef_bio.background: Nepal STATION opened in 2017 as what is described as Nagoya's first authentic Nepalese cuisine specialist restaurant, in the Marunouchi area. The concept grew from the reality that many so-called Indian curry restaurants in Japan are actually Nepalese-run — this shop drops the Indian-restaurant disguise entirely and serves the real Nepali table. It has since been selected for Tabelog's Asian-Ethnic EAST '100 Best' list (2022 and 2024).
chef_bio.philosophy: Present Nepali food as it actually exists in Nepal — regional, rice-centred, and spice-forward — rather than the adapted Indian-restaurant version familiar to Japanese diners.
chef_bio.specialty: Daal Bhat Set (two curries with rice, free refills of rice and lentil curry) and Samay Baji (a traditional Newari ethnic platter); the menu also runs to rarer items such as goat-brain curry.

anecdotes.text: The blog 名古屋単身ライフ describes Nepal STATION as Nagoya's first genuine Nepalese specialist, noting that most 'Indian' restaurants in Japan are staffed and owned by Nepalese people, making this restaurant an honest expression of a cuisine that had been hiding in plain sight.

A blog review on シャルの甘美なる日々 describes the dining room as 'surprisingly spacious and elegantly refurbished with Western design blended with Nepalese touches,' creating an upscale ambience despite the narrow, ladder-like staircase entry — and highlights Samay Baji, a traditional Newari dish historically served at festivals.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 名古屋単身ライフ・シャルの甘美なる日々・ホットペッパー等で、2017年営業開始、名古屋初の本格ネパール料理専門店、丸の内、狭い階段を上った先の広く洗練された空間、ダルバートセット（ご飯・豆カレーおかわり自由）、ネワール族のサマエバジ、羊の脳みそカレー等を確認。食べログ アジア・エスニックEAST百名店（2022・2024）選出。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No information on dedicated fryers or separate prep areas for wheat-free dishes was found in any reviewed source. Cross-contamination risk is unknown and must be confirmed directly with staff.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Soy sauce is not a standard ingredient in Nepalese cooking; the cuisine relies on mustard oil, ghee, and spice blends rather than soy-based condiments. However, the restaurant also serves izakaya-style dishes which may use Japanese condiments containing wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The kitchen handles meat, egg, and dairy alongside vegetable dishes. No separation protocol has been publicly documented. Ask staff whether vegetable curries are cooked in shared pans.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The manager speaks fluent Japanese and can discuss menu contents. Staff are Nepalese nationals; complex allergy queries in English or detailed Japanese may require advance notice by phone (052-202-8802).

positives.text: Nepalese cuisine is inherently rice-centred (dal bhat, basmati rice) with many naturally vegetable- and legume-based dishes, offering more GF-friendly options than Indian-restaurant menus that rely on naan.
Tabelog lists a vegetarian menu (ベジタリアンメニューあり) and a health/wellness menu, indicating the kitchen is accustomed to accommodating plant-based diners.

cultural_comfort.note: All staff are Nepalese; the manager speaks fluent Japanese and can handle dietary questions, but front-of-house communication is mostly basic Japanese.

nagoya_hiro_nagoya.gf_detail: Yakiniku is inherently meat-forward, and some cuts may be served with tare (dipping sauce) that typically contains wheat-based soy sauce. The omakase course includes dishes such as chateaubriand wrapped in seaweed with miso, which carries gluten risk. No gluten-free menu or dedicated GF options are documented. The restaurant states that allergies should be communicated at reservation time and accommodations will be made "as much as possible," but celiac-safe preparation cannot be confirmed. Cross-contamination risk from shared grill surfaces is likely. Inquiry at reservation is essential.
nagoya_hiro_nagoya.vegan_detail: This is a premium beef-focused omakase restaurant with no plant-based course or vegan options. The entire concept centers on Chita beef and select meat cuts; no vegan accommodations are documented or implied.
nagoya_hiro_nagoya.notes: Owner-chef Azuma is in his early thirties. He majored in geography at university, but awakened to food culture while in the U.S. and switched to a culinary career. He deals directly with Chita beef producers and has a discerning eye for meat, being well-versed in everything from cattle breeding to husbandry.

chef_bio.origin: 名古屋市西区樋の口町。シャトー西の丸ビル2階に構える完全予約・紹介制の隠れ家的焼肉店。
chef_bio.background: オーナーシェフのHIRO氏は30代前半。大学では地理学を学びつつ、渡米中（カリフォルニア）に食文化に目覚めて料理の道へ転身。知多牛の生産農家と直接取引し、自らの審美眼で肉を選び抜く。
chef_bio.philosophy: 肉の旬を見極め、最高の状態で提供すること。シェフ自らが炭火で焼き、産地・生産者・部位の解説を交えてもてなす。「訪れた人だけが知る隠れ家」というコンセプトで、1日1〜2組限定の濃密な体験を提供する。
chef_bio.specialty: 知多牛のシャトーブリアンを中心とした完全オマカセコース。シャトーブリアンの海苔巻き（万能ねぎ・味噌添え）が看板料理。1コースで約500gの肉を使い、ポワント（フィレの希少部位）など希少カットも登場する。

anecdotes.text: 地理学を学びながらも、渡米中に食文化に触れて料理の世界へ転身。知多牛の農家と直接パートナーシップを結び、産地から肉質を知り尽くした審美眼でコースを構成している。
シャトーブリアンを海苔で巻き、万能ねぎと味噌を添えた看板料理は、店を訪れた常連だけが知る一皿として語り継がれている。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログおよび名古屋焼肉セレクションによると、オーナーシェフHIRO氏は30代前半、大学で地理学を学びつつ渡米中（カリフォルニア）に食文化に目覚めて料理へ。知多牛農家と直接取引し、完全紹介・会員制で1日1〜2組限定。シャトーブリアンの海苔巻きが看板。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 共用の炭火グリルを使用するオマカーセ店であり、グルテン含有食材（醤油ベースのたれ、味噌など）との接触リスクが排除できない。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: 焼肉のたれや味噌など、小麦を含む調味料が使用されるオマカーセコースであり、グルテンフリー醤油の使用は確認されていない。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 完全な肉料理専門店のため、植物性食材のみのコースは提供されておらず、ヴィーガン対応は不可能。

staff_allergy_handling.text: アレルギーや苦手な食材は予約時に伝えれば「できる限り対応する」とされているが、セリアック病レベルの完全除去保証は確認できない。予約時の事前相談が必須。

positives.text: 完全紹介制・完全オマカーセのため、予約時に食の制約を細かく伝える機会があり、シェフが個別対応を検討できる環境にある。

cultural_comfort.note: 完全紹介制・会員制で、既存客からの紹介なしでは予約不可。日本語対応が前提の非常に敷居の高い完全オマカーセ店。

nagoya_mendokoro_ippachi.gf_detail: Every noodle on the menu — kishimen, udon, and soba — contains wheat. Breaded and fried items (tonkatsu, karaage, tempura, fry sets) add further wheat exposure. The kitchen uses tamari soy sauce for seasoning, which is traditionally lower in wheat than standard shoyu but is not certified gluten-free here. No dedicated gluten-free options are offered and cross-contamination with wheat throughout the kitchen is essentially certain. Not appropriate for celiac diners.
nagoya_mendokoro_ippachi.vegan_detail: All noodle broths are made with muro-bushi (dried horse mackerel) dashi — a fish-based stock — and most dishes feature meat, egg, or seafood. There are no identifiable vegan dishes on the menu. Chilled tofu and edamame appear as side options but share a kitchen with extensive animal products and the broth base is fish.
nagoya_mendokoro_ippachi.notes: [Mom & Pop] Founded in Showa 1 (1926) in Nishi Ward, Nagoya, めん処 一八 has been serving kishimen and Nagoya comfort food from the same address for roughly a century. The restaurant is now run by the third generation of the founding family, who have maintained the original recipes and ingredient

chef_bio.origin: 名古屋市西区新道（昭和元年・1926年創業）
chef_bio.background: Founded in Showa 1 (1926) in Nishi Ward, Nagoya, めん処 一八 has been serving kishimen and Nagoya comfort food from the same neighbourhood for roughly a century. The restaurant is now run by the third generation of the founding family, who have faithfully maintained the original recipes and ingredients with minimal change.
chef_bio.philosophy: Earnest and honest preservation of predecessor recipes: the dashi is still drawn from muro-bushi (dried muro-aji), a house tradition passed down through generations, and seasoning relies on top-grade tamari soy sauce for clean umami with gentle sweetness.
chef_bio.specialty: 牛すじ月見きしめん and miso nikomi udon — flat Nagoya-style kishimen noodles in a muro-bushi dashi broth, finished with premium tamari soy sauce; the broth recipe is the house's defining inheritance from its founders.

anecdotes.text: The beef-tendon moon-viewing kishimen — braised beef tendon served over flat noodles with a soft egg — is the dish most often cited by food writers as the reason to make a special trip to this century-old shop.

The shop states its broth is drawn from muro-bushi, a tradition inherited from the previous generation and described as giving the soup a deep richness and sweetness well-suited to kishimen and miso nikomi udon.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイトによると昭和元年（1926）西区新道で創業、3代目が継承。出汁は先代から受け継ぐむろ節でとり、たまり醤油を使用。牛すじ月見きしめん・味噌煮込みうどんが看板。

gf_cross_contamination.text: All noodles (kishimen, udon, soba) are wheat-based and cooked in the same kitchen. Tempura, tonkatsu, karaage, and other breaded items are also on the menu, making wheat cross-contamination near-certain throughout the kitchen.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The kitchen uses tamari soy sauce (たまり醤油) as its primary seasoning, which is traditionally wheat-reduced compared to standard shoyu, but no gluten-free certification is claimed and standard soy sauce use cannot be ruled out for all dishes.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The dashi base is muro-bushi (fish-derived), used throughout the noodle broths. No vegan broth alternative is offered. Shared cooking equipment with meat, seafood, and egg dishes throughout.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy-handling information or allergy menu is mentioned on the official website or Tabelog listing. The restaurant does not appear to cater to dietary restrictions; diners with serious allergies should call ahead (052-571-0485).

positives.text: Use of tamari soy sauce (たまり醤油) rather than standard wheat-heavy shoyu is a notable ingredient choice, though it does not make the restaurant gluten-free.

cultural_comfort.note: Traditional neighborhood noodle shop with tatami seating and a Japanese-language-only menu; little to no English signage or staff English ability should be expected.

nagoya_unabun_unagi_no_unabun_h.gf_detail: Traditional unagi tare (kabayaki sauce) is made with wheat-containing soy sauce — standard for all eel preparations in Japan. No gluten-free or allergen-adapted options are listed anywhere. Cross-contamination risk from shared cooking surfaces and shared tare pot. No dedicated fryer info available. Celiacs should treat this as high-risk and contact the restaurant directly before visiting.
nagoya_unabun_unagi_no_unabun_h.vegan_detail: Entirely an eel (unagi) specialist. There are no plant-based dishes. The menu centers on hitsumabushi and unagi-don, with dashi-based soups. Nothing here suits a vegan diner.
nagoya_unabun_unagi_no_unabun_h.notes: [Mom & Pop] Unabun began as a long-established charcoal-grilled eel shop in the basement restaurant arcade of the Chunichi Building (中日ビル) in Sakae, where it operated for over 40 years. When the Chunichi Building was slated for demolition in early 2019, the shop relocated rather than close,

chef_bio.background: Unabun is a long-established charcoal-grilled eel shop (創業45年) that for more than four decades operated in the basement restaurant arcade of the Chunichi Building (中日ビル) in Sakae. When the Chunichi Building was slated for demolition in 2019, the shop relocated rather than close, reopening in April 2019 at its current address in Marunouchi — a short walk north up Otsu-dori from its former home.
chef_bio.philosophy: Accessible, no-frills charcoal-grilled eel grounded in the eel-trade adage 串打ち3年、裂き8年、焼きは一生 ('three years to skewer, eight years to fillet, a lifetime to grill') — the shop keeps prices down while maintaining the charcoal grill tradition.
chef_bio.specialty: Hitsumabushi — charcoal-grilled eel served in a wooden ohitsu vessel, eaten in three ways: plain, with condiments (wasabi, negi, nori), and as ochazuke with dashi poured over. A weekday-lunch unagi-don at around ¥1,050 makes this one of the more affordable eel options in the city.

anecdotes.text: After more than four decades in the Chunichi Building basement, the shop survived that landmark's 2019 demolition by securing a stand-alone space in nearby Marunouchi, winning praise from regulars who had feared it would disappear.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: ブログ・ホットペッパー等によると、栄の中日ビル地下で40年以上営業した炭火うなぎ専門店。中日ビル解体（2019）に伴い2019年4月に丸の内へ移転。創業45年、継ぎ足しのタレで炭火焼き。平日昼のうなぎ丼は約1,050円と手頃。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen information is published. Traditional kabayaki tare contains wheat-based soy sauce applied to all eel dishes; no wheat-free alternative is mentioned anywhere.
Shared cooking surfaces (charcoal grill) and communal tare pot are standard at this style of eel restaurant, creating cross-contamination risk.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Kabayaki sauce (tare) is the defining flavour element of all unagi dishes here; standard Japanese tare is made with wheat-containing soy sauce and mirin. No wheat-free soy sauce option is listed.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The entire menu is eel-based. There are no plant-based dishes, so vegan cross-contact is a moot point — the restaurant is simply not suitable for vegans.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy-handling policy or dedicated procedure is listed on any platform. Contact the restaurant directly (052-971-3148) well in advance if you have a wheat allergy.

positives.text: Completely non-smoking interior; small, consistent kitchen focused on a single ingredient, which limits the variety of allergen sources present.

cultural_comfort.note: A long-established local eel shop with Japanese-only menus and signage; staff are welcoming but English communication should not be expected.

nagoya_pivote.gf_detail: Teppanyaki French cuisine relies on French sauces and condiments; soy sauce use in marinades or sauces is unconfirmed. No gluten-free menu, dedicated fryer, or allergen information is advertised. Cross-contamination protocols are unknown. Guests with celiac disease should call ahead.
nagoya_pivote.vegan_detail: The menu is built around premium Japanese wagyu (Ozaki beef from Miyazaki) and seasonal animal proteins; vegetables are plentiful and a deliberate counterpoint, but no plant-only course is listed. Dashi type and hidden animal fats are unknown. Advance inquiry recommended.
nagoya_pivote.hours_raw: Mon 17:30–00:00 (next day) / Tue–Sat 11:30–13:00, 17:30–00:00 (next day) (L.O. 22:00) / closed Sun & holidays
nagoya_pivote.notes: Chef Satoh spent more than two decades mastering French cuisine, training at French restaurants in Gifu, then at establishments in Kobe, Tokyo, and Nagoya before opening Pivote in August 2014.

chef_bio.origin: 名古屋市西区那古野（四間道エリア）
chef_bio.background: Chef Satoh spent roughly two decades (22 years) mastering French cuisine — apprenticing live-in at a French restaurant in Gifu, then refining his craft at establishments in Kobe, Tokyo, and Nagoya before opening Pivote on 28 August 2014.
chef_bio.philosophy: To dissolve the heavy image of traditional teppanyaki by pairing premium grilled proteins with abundant farm-sourced seasonal vegetables, while cooking face-to-face with guests at the counter.
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase teppan courses centred on Ozaki beef from Miyazaki Prefecture — carefully selected sirloin and tender red-meat cuts cooked tableside on an iron griddle (about 17 seats).

anecdotes.text: Chef Satoh chose the quiet, warehouse-lined streets of Shikemichi for his restaurant specifically because of their nostalgic Showa atmosphere — close to Nagoya Station yet feeling removed from the city, which he felt matched the calm, intimate dining experience he wanted to create.

The counter ceiling was finished with a cat's-eye treatment to add warmth against the coldness of stainless steel — a deliberate design gesture to make guests comfortable while watching live teppan cooking.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: オトナの名古屋・名古の街インタビュー等によると、佐藤シェフは岐阜のフレンチで住み込み修業後、神戸・東京・名古屋で研鑽し計22年。2014年8月28日、四間道にピヴォーテを開業。宮崎・尾崎牧場の尾崎牛を中心とした鉄板フレンチ、約17席。

cultural_comfort.note: Counter-only omakase with the chef cooking directly in front of guests — interaction is warm but menus and signage are in Japanese; English assistance is not advertised.

nagoya_fukurou.gf_detail: Standard Japanese izakaya kitchen: soy sauce (wheat-containing), mirin, and tempura batter are ubiquitous. Mixed-fry (フライ) dishes were noted in reviews, indicating shared frying oil is very likely. No gluten-free menu, dedicated fryer, or allergy communication system has been mentioned in any source. Guests with celiac disease should contact the restaurant directly before visiting.
nagoya_fukurou.vegan_detail: This is a seafood-forward izakaya with a dashi-based kitchen — hidden fish stock (鰹だし・昆布だし) is standard across virtually every dish. No plant-based or vegan options are indicated anywhere on the menu or in reviews. Vegans should contact the restaurant in advance, but meaningful accommodation is unlikely.
nagoya_fukurou.notes: [Mom & Pop] 福ろう opened on June 14, 2026 in Nishi Ward's Hinokuchi-cho, near Nagoya Castle, as the relocated successor to 梟 (Fukurou) — a long-running izakaya that operated for roughly 20 years in the Shinsakae/Higashi Ward area. The original 梟 was awarded a Michelin Plate in the Michelin Gui

chef_bio.background: 福ろう opened on June 14, 2026 in Nishi Ward's Hinokuchi-cho, near Nagoya Castle, as the relocated successor to 梟 (Fukurou) — a long-running izakaya that operated for roughly 20 years in the Shinsakae/Higashi Ward (Aoi) area. The original 梟 was awarded a Michelin Plate in the Michelin Guide Aichi/Gifu/Mie 2019 special edition, recognising its quality among Nagoya's izakaya scene.
chef_bio.philosophy: A small, intimate counter-focused izakaya that prizes fresh fish, well-chosen drinks, and a relaxed neighbourhood atmosphere over scale or fanfare.
chef_bio.specialty: Fresh seasonal seafood — sashimi platters featuring whatever the market offers that day (flounder, mackerel and other daily catch), alongside carefully selected Japanese sake, shochu and wine.

anecdotes.text: The original Higashi-Ward location earned a Michelin Plate in the 2019 Michelin Guide Aichi/Gifu/Mie special edition — one of only four izakayas awarded a Plate that year (seven izakayas appeared in that edition in total, the other three as Bib Gourmand).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログおよびミシュランまとめによると、2026年6月14日、西区樋の口町（名古屋城近く）に移転オープン。前身の居酒屋「梟」は東区葵（新栄）で約20年営業し、ミシュランガイド愛知2019でプレートを獲得（掲載居酒屋は計7軒＝ビブ3・プレート4）。鮮魚の刺身と日本酒・焼酎・ワインが中心、18席。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Mixed-fry (フライ) dishes appear on the menu, strongly suggesting shared frying oil. No dedicated fryer is mentioned.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard izakaya kitchen; wheat-containing soy sauce is used throughout Japanese pub cooking and no tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is noted anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish-forward kitchen; dashi from katsuobushi (bonito) or niboshi is standard across hot dishes, soups, and simmered items. No plant-based alternatives noted.

positives.text: Non-smoking throughout the entire venue — a comfort for sensitive diners.

cultural_comfort.note: A quiet neighborhood izakaya with no English menu or English-speaking staff noted; ordering confidence in Japanese is strongly recommended.

nagoya_yoi_usagi.gf_detail: Standard izakaya fare heavily reliant on wheat-based soy sauce (shoyu) in marinades, yakitori tare, and cooking sauces. Fried items (karaage, shrimp mayo, hand wings) use wheat-flour batter. No gluten-free labeling, dedicated fryer, or allergen accommodation mentioned. Cross-contamination risk is high in a 12-seat counter kitchen. Celiacs should call ahead and ask in detail before visiting.
nagoya_yoi_usagi.vegan_detail: Standard izakaya menu with no declared vegan options. Many dishes involve animal products (pork, chicken karaage, shrimp mayo, sashimi). Some nominally plant-based items (fried tofu, rolled egg, grilled rice balls) likely use dashi stock with bonito or are cooked in shared oil. No vegan labeling or accommodation mentioned on Tabelog or the menu page.
nagoya_yoi_usagi.hours_raw: 15:00–00:00 (food L.O. 23:00, drink L.O. 23:30), open Mon–Sun & holidays, irregular days off

Despite the international background, the current menu is entirely standard Japanese pub fare — the owner has noted 'ミャンマー感ゼロ' (zero Myanmar c

chef_bio.background: A small, 12-seat izakaya (8 counter, 4 table) opened on May 15, 2026 in the Oshikiri neighborhood of Nagoya's Nishi Ward, run by an owner originally from Myanmar. Despite the international background, the current menu is entirely standard Japanese pub fare — a reviewer notes 'ミャンマー感ゼロ' (zero Myanmar character) for now, with the owner planning to introduce Burmese dishes in the future.
chef_bio.philosophy: A relaxed neighborhood watering hole designed for post-work drop-ins and solo diners, with a welcoming counter atmosphere. Affordable drink-and-dish sets and an approachable menu are the core proposition.
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-braised slow-cooked pork (煮豚) — deeply flavoured and tender — served alongside affordable drink-and-dish set combinations.

anecdotes.text: A reviewer describes the current menu as 'a pleasantly ordinary, delicious izakaya with zero Myanmar character,' while noting the owner plans to add Burmese dishes as the shop matures.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログによると、2026年5月15日、西区押切にオープンした12席（カウンター8・テーブル4）の居酒屋。オーナーはミャンマー出身だが現メニューは『ミャンマー感ゼロ』、将来的にミャンマー料理を追加予定。柔らかい煮豚が看板、飲み物付きセットが中心。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen or cross-contamination information is published. The small open kitchen (12 seats) shared across fried, grilled, and sauced dishes poses a meaningful cross-contamination risk for gluten-sensitive diners.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Wheat-based soy sauce is used throughout the menu in yakitori tare, marinades, and cooked preparations. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fried items share oil with meat and seafood. Bonito-based dashi is standard in Japanese izakaya stocks and not flagged as absent here.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy handling policy is described on Tabelog. Phone contact (052-990-0476) is the recommended route for dietary inquiries before visiting.

positives.text: English menu and English-capable staff listed on Tabelog, lowering the language barrier for communicating dietary needs.

cultural_comfort.note: Tabelog lists English menu and English-speaking staff available; the owner, who is from Myanmar, runs a welcoming solo-diner-friendly counter.

nagoya_sake_bar_marutani.gf_detail: A standard Japanese izakaya kitchen — soy sauce (wheat-containing) appears throughout grilled dishes, simmered dishes, dressings, and course menus. Tempura is on the menu. No gluten-free labeling exists anywhere on the site. Wheat-based dashi and soy is endemic. Celiac diners must contact the restaurant directly before visiting; cross-contamination risk in a shared kitchen is high.
nagoya_sake_bar_marutani.vegan_detail: Tabelog listing notes a vegan course is available but requires reservation at least 3 days in advance. The standard menu is heavily meat- and seafood-focused (duck, chicken, beef, cod, eel, squid, shrimp). Hidden dashi (fish stock) is likely in many dishes not labeled vegan. The vegan course must be requested explicitly at time of booking; do not assume any a la carte items are vegan without asking.
nagoya_sake_bar_marutani.hours_raw: Sun–Thu: 17:00–23:00 (food LO 22:00, drinks LO 22:30); Fri–Sat and day before holidays: 17:00–00:00 (food LO 23:00, drinks LO 23:30)
